cases.description: Two genuine alternatives are on the table: Option A (Redis cache in front of pricing.py) and Option B (Postgres index on the pricing table) -- both concrete, not a strawman.
cases.grounding: engine/report.py parsed 2 options labeled 'Option A' and 'Option B' from explicit 'Option X:' markers.

cases.description: Both options score blast_radius_score=14 and impact all three modules in the report, including engine/checkout.py, which neither option text actually mentions. This is a real path-prefix keyword collision, not evidence both options touch checkout.py: every module path here starts with 'engine/', and 'engine' itself is extracted as a keyword from both option texts, so it path-matches every module and inflates the blast-radius score regardless of relevance. The number should not be trusted at face value for this fixture -- only engine/pricing.py and engine/database.py are plausible real targets.
cases.grounding: impact_scorer.py's _extract_keywords has no stopword for 'engine'; every module here shares that path prefix, matching the same coincidental-substring class of limitation already documented for feature-planner (L14) and root-cause-analyzer (L19).

cases.description: Option A: lower latency, higher operational cost (new Redis cluster), fully reversible. Option B: lower operational cost, smaller latency gain, effectively one-way (schema index). Neither changes authentication or access control.
cases.grounding: Decision text's third paragraph states both tradeoffs and reversibility explicitly for each option.
